blocks.x: Cloud, Edge & Platform applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Education & Research, cloud, edge & platform engineering builds the runtime for everything else we do: hybrid and multicloud architecture, cloud-native modernization of legacy estates, edge and distributed infrastructure for latency-critical operations, sre and reliability engineering, internal developer platforms, finops, and mission-critical high-performance systems. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: hybrid & multicloud architecture, cloud-native & legacy modernization, edge computing & distributed infrastructure — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Twinverse with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Labs buy cloud haphazardly; HPC queues and cloud spend lack governance, and research data governance varies by department.
LMS, SIS, attendance and support-service data never meet; at-risk students surface at failure, not at drift.
Generative tools flood campuses with no policy infrastructure; detection arms races erode trust while legitimate assistive use goes ungoverned.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Cloud, Edge & Platform Engineering tower — Hybrid & Multicloud Architecture, Cloud-Native & Legacy Modernization, Edge Computing & Distributed Infrastructure, SRE & Reliability Engineering as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: Accessibility mandates (ADA/EN 301 549) obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: The estate as designed system: landing zones, network fabric and workload placement by economics.
Retire the legacy tax: strangler-pattern modernization with measurable unit economics.
Compute where the physics is: edge estate for plants, stores, vehicles and grids.
Reliability as product: SLOs, error budgets and incident discipline that engineers actually follow.
HPC/cloud burst with queue governance and cost telemetry (throughput up 2-5x per funding unit)
Departmental cloud showback with commitment strategy (waste visible and reduced)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: Accessibility mandates (ADA/EN 301 549) and Export controls on research. Dual-use technology data governance. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
